correctness.rationale: The derivative gives squarefreeness exactly for a²≠4; the degree-ten monic model is genus four with two points at infinity. The inversion quotient has coordinates t=x+x^{-1} and v=y(x+1)/x³, with v²=(t+2)(t⁵−5t³+5t+a), and these generate the fixed field because x solves a quadratic over them. The trivial rotation eigenspace in H¹ vanishes by the genus-zero rotation quotient. The inverse-character eigenspaces are swapped by inversion; Frobenius commutes with both operators, so the determinant on each such pair is the square of the determinant on its inversion-invariants, giving the square Weil numerator via the genus-two quotient. Independent direct counts of C in degrees 1 through 4 reproduce the full squared polynomials: in the five table rows they are (4,114,1084,14314), (24,154,1224,14634), (14,204,1274,13924), (14,164,1334,15124), (4,194,1564,14314). E has 10 rational points. Only the last Q is an elliptic square, and comparing the first two coefficients of Q(T) and Q(−T) distinguishes the ten spectra. The point-count-only assertion in frozen RESULT.md line 38 overstates the original check: C counts in degrees one and two do not by themselves certify the whole degree-eight equality. The cohomological proof establishes it, and independent degree-three and degree-four counts supply the full numeric check here. For the geometric assertion, only diagonal exponents are divisible by five; extraction in (z²+az+1)^5 gives coefficients of z² and z⁴ equal to 5−a² and 5a⁴−3a²−1, paired by reciprocity. For h₂/5, the associated quadratic in a² has nonsquare discriminant 6 and roots in F₁₂₁ of norm 2, a nonsquare in F₁₁. Hence neither root is a square in F₁₂₁ and the quartic is irreducible, giving the degree-four orbit. The h₁ roots ±4 are simple, disjoint from that orbit, and all six roots are smooth parameters. The paired diagonal entries give determinant multiplicity two; rank and stable rank coincide because iteration preserves diagonal support over the perfect geometric field, including with the Cartier scalar roots.
